questions.question: When must you show proof of insurance to police?

options.text: Only if you are in a crash.
If you are in a crash or stopped for a ticket.
Only if you are stopped and given a ticket.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are in a crash or stopped for a ticket.
questions.explanation: You must carry proof of insurance when you drive. Show your proof of insurance and license to an officer when asked after a traffic stop or crash.

questions.question: You are driving on the freeway behind a large truck. How should you drive?

options.text: Close behind the truck in bad weather because the driver can see farther ahead.
Farther behind the truck than you would behind a regular car.
No more than one car length behind so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther behind the truck than you would behind a regular car.
questions.explanation: If you drive too close behind a truck, the driver cannot see you in their mirrors. Tailgating is dangerous because you lose your safety cushion if the truck stops suddenly.

questions.question: Which of the following slows down traffic?

options.text: Slowing down to look at a crash.
Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.
Using public transportation instead of driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down to look at a crash.
questions.explanation: Slowing down to look at crashes causes traffic jams and should be avoided.

questions.question: At a red light with a green arrow, when can you proceed in the direction of the arrow?

options.text: After you come to a complete stop.
When the light changes.
When you are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear.
questions.explanation: You can proceed in the direction of a green arrow if you are in the correct lane. Always yield to pedestrians and other vehicles already in the intersection before turning.

questions.question: Where are a truck's blind spots?

options.text: Directly behind the truck.
On the left side of the cab.
On the left side of the cab and directly behind the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left side of the cab and directly behind the truck.
questions.explanation: Trucks have large blind spots. The driver cannot see your car if you drive too close behind or to the side. If you cannot see the driver's face in their side mirror, they cannot see you.

questions.question: When passing another car, when is it safe to return to your lane?

options.text: When the other driver signals you to move back.
When you look over your shoulder and see the car behind you.
When you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When you can see both headlights of the car you passed in your rearview mirror, there is a safe gap between you. Then it is safe to return to your lane.

questions.question: If you park your car in an unusual spot, what should you do?

options.text: Leave your reverse lights on.
Make sure drivers approaching from any direction can see your car.
Park five feet from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure drivers approaching from any direction can see your car.
questions.explanation: Wherever you park, make sure your car is visible to drivers approaching from all directions so it does not become a hazard.

questions.question: If you are about to be hit from behind, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Release your seat belt.
Brace yourself.
Press your head against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release your seat belt.
questions.explanation: Keep your seat belt on. Brace yourself by pressing against your seat and putting your head against the head restraint to prevent injury. Hold the steering wheel firmly and be ready to brake.

questions.question: How do stopping distance and crash severity relate to vehicle speed?

options.text: They decrease as speed increases.
They are not affected by speed.
They increase as speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: They increase as speed increases.
questions.explanation: Stopping distances are longer and crashes are more severe at higher speeds.

questions.question: If you had an argument and are angry, what should you do before driving?

options.text: Play loud music so you won't think about the argument.
Take a few minutes to calm down.
Drive on the highway to let off steam.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down.
questions.explanation: Emotions affect your ability to drive safely. Give yourself time to calm down before driving so you can focus on the road.

questions.question: What do construction zone signs usually look like?

options.text: Square or rectangular with white and red coloring.
Round or octagonal with black and yellow coloring.
Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black coloring.

questions.correctAnswerText: Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black coloring.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs have an orange background with black letters or symbols. These signs appear on the right side of the road, or on both sides on divided highways.

questions.question: How can you check your blind spot when changing lanes?

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Use your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Mirrors cannot show all areas. Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder to see your blind spots.

questions.question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?

options.text: In an intersection if there are no oncoming cars.
Wherever signs and road markings allow passing.
On a curve if there are no oncoming cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wherever signs and road markings allow passing.
questions.explanation: Never pass in intersections, parking lot entrances, or alleys. Never pass on curves or hills where you cannot see ahead. Only pass where signs and road markings allow it and when you have enough space to do so safely.

questions.question: Is backing your vehicle dangerous?

options.text: Yes, it is always dangerous.
Only if you have a helper.
Only in large vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is always dangerous.
questions.explanation: Backing up is always dangerous because you cannot see behind your vehicle easily. Use extra caution when backing up.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in fog?

options.text: High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
Low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect back at you, making it harder to see.

questions.question: In Arizona, vehicles must have liability insurance:

options.text: Only when driving on an interstate.
At all times.
Only when a minor is driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: Every vehicle in Arizona must have liability insurance. The policy must be based in Arizona and cover where the vehicle is mainly driven.

questions.question: To make a right turn correctly, you should:

options.text: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the centerline.
Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right curb.
Approach the corner from the right lane, then move toward the middle of the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right curb.
questions.explanation: Before turning right, signal to warn other drivers. Slow down and stay as close as possible to the right curb as you approach the intersection.

questions.question: After a train passes at a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Wait for the signal lights to stop flashing.
Watch for a second train.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: After a train passes, another train may be coming on another track. Do not go until all gates are lifted and all warning lights stop flashing.

questions.question: Yellow lines separate:

options.text: Traffic lanes on one-way streets.
Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark the center of two-way roads. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass. A broken yellow line means you may pass only if it is safe.

questions.question: You should drive on the shoulder to pass another car:

options.text: If the car ahead is turning left.
Never.
If the shoulder is wide enough.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never pass on the shoulder. The other driver will not expect you there and may pull onto the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Service sign.
Regulatory sign.
Warning sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to dangerous conditions ahead, such as a turn, steep hill, or hazard that needs your attention.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Have the right-of-way over oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left, let oncoming traffic and pedestrians go first. Turn only when the intersection is clear and the signal allows it.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, you should:

options.text: Release the gas pedal.
Brake as hard as possible.
Turn off the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, release the gas pedal or brakes to regain balance. Steer in the direction of the skid to regain control.

questions.question: Hydroplaning is when tires slide on water instead of the road. To prevent it in wet weather, you should:

options.text: Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Slow down.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it starts raining.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Slow down on wet pavement to prevent it.

questions.question: When you have a green light and pedestrians are in the intersection, you should:

options.text: Yield to the pedestrians.
Have the right-of-way over pedestrians.
Pedestrians must wait for you to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to the pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, yield to pedestrians already in the intersection. Always yield when turning on a steady green light.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Stop as quickly as possible.
Stop and proceed only when the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: At a flashing yellow light, slow down and go carefully. You do not need to stop completely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down or stop.
Stop if necessary.
You must come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An octagonal sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop and only proceed when it is safe. Stop at the marked line, or before the crosswalk or intersection if there is no line.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow-moving vehicle.
Road work area.
Traffic light ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle.
questions.explanation: This sign is placed on vehicles that move slowly.

questions.question: On a highway next to a broken white line, you may:

options.text: Not cross the line to pass.
Cross the line to pass and change lanes.
Cross the line to change lanes only if you are in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross the line to pass and change lanes.
questions.explanation: White dashed lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. You can cross a dashed white line to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: A red arrow pointing right on a traffic light means you:

options.text: Can turn after slowing and checking for traffic.
Cannot turn until the light turns green.
Can turn after coming to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot turn until the light turns green.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means stop. You must wait until a green light or green arrow appears. Do not turn against a red arrow.
